summary: Radar for 2026-10-27, GLP-1 focus. Only one item is truly new and early: Vanda's Phase 3 Study 3601. Tradipitant, an NK-1 anti-nausea drug, cut vomiting after a single 1 mg semaglutide dose: 43.0% vomited on tradipitant versus 58.5% on placebo (n=142 versus 164). HCPLive covered it on Oct 27, and almost no creators have yet. It doesn't qualify as Lane C because it isn't a next-gen GLP-1, so it goes to a 13:00 Short and serves as a fresh hook for the Lane A side-effects videos. No Lane C long-form qualifies today. UBT251's Cell Metabolism paper (Oct 26) reports results first made public on March 25, 2026, so it gets a Short only. Retatrutide sleep apnea is now peaking (Gizmodo, Medscape, EMJ). Lilly's Q3 call on Oct 29 is the next possible Lane C trigger: it may bring retatrutide, EloraTZP or orforglipron updates, so check first-report dates on the day. The long-form slots should follow the playbook's Lane A queue, each refreshed by this week's news: bones and muscle (Arch Osteoporos review, Oct 23), protein (Food & Wine protein-trend piece, Oct 27), stopping (SURMOUNT-4 plus new persistence papers), hair loss (Med Sci cutaneous adverse-event systematic review, Oct 9), and a search-style 'side effects: which is easier?' video hooked on tradipitant. Other Shorts this week: the Connecticut AG settlement with Made-in-China over 'research-grade' GLP-1s (ABC/GMA, Oct 27) as the week's single gray-market 'what's confirmed' Short; ACOG's pregnancy guidance (Medscape, Oct 27); semaglutide and alcohol; the Wegovy NAION signal; and the 'GLP-1 companion' supplement credibility gap. Thanksgiving is the seasonal evergreen, peaking Nov 20–27, so prep it now. Microdosing and retatrutide 'sourcing' stay rejected. Caveat: PubMed abstracts were behind a CAPTCHA, so the contents of the cutaneous and lymphedema papers are unverified and must be checked by the researcher.

candidates.topic: Tradipitant cut vomiting after semaglutide in a Phase 3 trial (Vanda Study 3601, HCPLive Oct 27, 2026): 43.0% vs 58.5% vomited after a single 1 mg semaglutide dose (n=142 vs 164)
candidates.angle: 'Could a pill make GLP-1 nausea easier? What this new trial actually tested.' Give the honest scope: a single 1 mg semaglutide challenge dose, not weekly treatment. Vomiting was the main measure; nausea alone wasn't reported. Tirzepatide wasn't tested, it isn't approved for this use, and the FDA meeting isn't until 2027. Then give what helps today (smaller meals, stopping at full, avoiding greasy food, talking to your prescriber). Loop ending back to 'not yet, but here's what works now.'
keywords: how to stop nausea on Wegovy
candidates.why_now: The topline came out Oct 27, with only HCPLive and investor press so far. Nausea is our audience's biggest side-effect worry (the nausea Short reached 130 on YouTube and 120 on Instagram), and the Oct 22 reviews on how trials under-measure nausea give us context. Consumer outlets haven't picked it up yet.

evidence.signal: Phase 3 RCT, n=306. Any vomiting 43.0% vs 58.5% (P=.006). Vomiting plus worst nausea ≥3: 33.1% vs 50.6%. FDA meeting expected in 2027 ahead of an sNDA
Primary source. Extreme vomiting 2.8% vs 14.6% (post hoc, site-adjusted)

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and your bones and muscle: the new Arch Osteoporos systematic review (Oct 23, 2026) plus the SURMOUNT-1 body-scan substudy
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form, top of the playbook queue. Open on a 'you' scenario: 'You've lost 40 lb on tirzepatide. Is some of it bone or muscle?' Give the answer in 15 s: about a quarter to a third of the lost weight was lean mass in the body-scan substudy, the share of fat-free mass in the body went up, and bone data are mixed and mostly from GLP-1 agonists in general. Then cover what helps: protein, resistance training, and asking your prescriber about bone checks if you're at risk. Honest uncertainty tone.
